# Lab 11.14: Enable Layer 7 Inspection

## What We Are Going to Do
Turn on Cloud NGFW Enterprise intrusion prevention for a VPC, and block a test attack against a web server.

## Steps

1. **Know the cost first.** Firewall endpoints are billed per hour and take about 20 minutes to create. Delete them as soon as you finish. This lab reuses `fw-vpc` and the `lab-nfp` policy from Lab 11.10, so run it before that lab's cleanup.

2. **Create a threat prevention security profile and group** at the organization.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud network-security security-profiles threat-prevention create lab-tp \
  --organization=ORG_ID --location=global

gcloud network-security security-profile-groups create lab-spg \
  --organization=ORG_ID --location=global \
  --threat-prevention-profile=organizations/ORG_ID/locations/global/securityProfiles/lab-tp</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **Create a firewall endpoint in a zone** and associate it with your VPC.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud network-security firewall-endpoints create lab-fe \
  --organization=ORG_ID --zone=us-central1-a --billing-project=$PROJECT_ID

gcloud network-security firewall-endpoint-associations create lab-fea \
  --zone=us-central1-a --network=fw-vpc --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --endpoint=organizations/ORG_ID/locations/us-central1-a/firewallEndpoints/lab-fe</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **Send web traffic through inspection.** Add a rule with the `apply_security_profile_group` action to the network firewall policy from Lab 11.10.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud compute network-firewall-policies rules create 150 --firewall-policy=lab-nfp \
  --global-firewall-policy --direction=INGRESS \
  --action=apply_security_profile_group \
  --security-profile-group=//networksecurity.googleapis.com/organizations/ORG_ID/locations/global/securityProfileGroups/lab-spg \
  --src-ip-ranges=10.40.0.0/24 --layer4-configs=tcp:80 --enable-logging</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **Run a web server and a client** on two VMs in `us-central1-a` in `fw-vpc`. On the server install `apache2`. From the client send a known test pattern:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">curl -m5 "http://SERVER_IP/cgi-bin/../../../..//bin/cat%20/etc/passwd"</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   The request is dropped.

6. **See the threat.** Go to **Network Security → Threats**. The event shows the threat name, severity and action **Deny**.

7. **Clean up the paid parts first.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">gcloud network-security firewall-endpoint-associations delete lab-fea --zone=us-central1-a --project=$PROJECT_ID
gcloud network-security firewall-endpoints delete lab-fe --zone=us-central1-a --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud network-security security-profile-groups delete lab-spg --organization=ORG_ID --location=global
gcloud network-security security-profiles threat-prevention delete lab-tp --organization=ORG_ID --location=global</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Then delete the two test VMs and run the cleanup from Lab 11.10.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Inspection | Inline, by the firewall endpoint |
| Test attack | Blocked and shown in Threats |
| Tier | Cloud NGFW Enterprise |
| Cost | Hourly per endpoint, delete when done |
